inference: A cold boot with this owner-demonstrated ISR PoE supply attached from power-on reproduces the C8235 detection failure. It is not merely an empty global CLI before initialization: controller presence and budget remain unavailable after the module is ready. This narrows the problem to C8235 circuitry/power/detection or supply compatibility; it does not distinguish absent/failed circuitry, incompatible startup/connection, or firmware/FPGA interpretation.
limits: No measured PoE rail voltage inside the powered C8235.
No raw hardware status flags or verified external enable/handshake mechanism.
No full capacity or cross-platform compatibility proof for the brick.
Diagnostic firmware causal role unproven; successful boot does not qualify every peripheral.
Historical PHOTOS2/IMG_1293.jpeg reviewed again, bound to A by photo-inspection.json; no component-function assignment or physical absence proof from this overview.
